THE LITURGICAL YEAR AT SAINT JOSEPH PARISH
Our parish community keeps the liturgical year through liturgy, devotion, worship, adoration, and charity, guided by church law and papal law. Pastor, parish vicar, deacon, catechist, sponsor, and laity share each Mass and rite.

Advent devotions begin the year. Each catechist prepares every child, parent, and student for baptism, confirmation, and Eucharist, while our permanent deacon leads the Divine Office, Angelus, litany, and novena in the chapel.

Christmas devotions honor the Incarnation and Nativity of the Messiah, born of Mary in Bethlehem. On the Baptism of the Lord, our pastor baptizes infants with chrism.

Lenten devotions call clergy and laity to repentance, contrition, humility, and penance. A priest hears sacramental confession, grants absolution, and assigns acts of penance. The Way of the Cross recalls the Crucifixion and entombment; a Palm Sunday entry and religious procession open Holy Week, and the Last Supper recalls the institution of the Eucharist.

Easter devotions proclaim the Resurrection, Ascension of Christ, and Pentecost, when the Paraclete descended. Through RCIA, adults receive baptism, chrismation, and Holy Communion. Our diocesan bishop confers confirmation at the cathedral; an auxiliary bishop ordains a transitional deacon through Holy Orders.

Healing sacraments continue year-round. Our chaplain brings last anointing to the hospital chapel, and reconciliation restores communion. Matrimony unites each spouse in Christian marriage. A funeral ends with burial, interment, or cremation in a consecrated cemetery.

This bulletin cites Scripture, the Decalogue, the Beatitudes, and Catholic social teaching on faith, hope, chastity, prudence, justice, and forgiveness, so that patience, meekness, and compassion guide every family. We pray the Holy Rosary, Hail Mary, Memorare, and Glory Be during Eucharistic adoration of the Blessed Sacrament, honoring the Trinity.

Every volunteer, donor, benefactor, trustee, secretary, and treasurer helps. A religious sister, prior, and nun from a nearby monastery, abbey, convent, and friary join our youth minister, church rector, and lay minister at the basilica and shrine. Our seminary, college, and parish church welcome each immigrant and refugee from Italy, Ireland, Mexico, and Poland. We remain in communion with the Pope, the Holy See, our archbishop, and the universal church.

concepts.folio_definition: The Holy Rosary is a Marian devotional prayer that meditates on the mysteries of Christ’s life through repeated vocal prayer and contemplation. It combines the recitation of the Hail Mary with reflection on the Gospel, leading the faithful to deeper union with Christ through Mary.
folio_examples: Each decade of the rosary centers on a Gospel mystery.
Families often pray the rosary together.

Start by making the sign of the Cross:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
Amen.

Then recite the Creed:
I believe in God, the Father almighty,
Creator of heaven and earth,
and in Jesus Christ, His only Son, our Lord.
He was conceived by the Holy Spirit,
and born of the Virgin Mary.
He suffered under Pontius Pilate,
was crucified, died and was buried.
He descended into hell.
On the third day He rose again.
He ascended into heaven,
and is seated at the right hand of God the Father Almighty.
He will come again to judge the living and the dead.
I believe in the Holy Spirit,
the Holy Catholic Church,
the communion of saints,
the forgiveness of sins,
the resurrection of the body,
and life everlasting.

Then say 1 "Our Father", 3 "Hail Mary's" for the virtues of Faith, Hope and Charity; and then 1 "Glory Be":
Our Father, Who art in heaven, Hallowed be Thy Name. Thy Kingdom come, Thy Will be done, On earth as it is in Heaven. Give us this day, our daily bread, And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.

Hail Mary, Full of Grace, The Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners now, and at the hour of death. 

Glory Be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end.


The Rosary is divided into three parts, each having five mysteries. While meditating on the Mysteries, recite for each Mystery:
1 "Our Father"
10 "Hail Mary's" and
1 "Glory Be"

After each Mystery the "Fatima Prayer" is said.
O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fire of hell, lead all souls to heaven, especially those who are in most need of Thy mercy.

All together this makes up one decade.

After the completion of the five mysteries (five decades), the "Hail Holy Queen" is said:
Hail, holy Queen, mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness, and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us, and after this our exile show us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

In the Name of the Father, and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
The rosary invites meditation on the mysteries of Christ’s life.

sentence_pos.text:
THE LITURGICAL YEAR AT SAINT JOSEPH PARISH
Our parish community keeps the liturgical year through liturgy, devotion, worship, adoration, and charity, guided by church law and papal law.
Pastor, parish vicar, deacon, catechist, sponsor, and laity share each Mass and rite.
Advent devotions begin the year.
Each catechist prepares every child, parent, and student for baptism, confirmation, and Eucharist, while our permanent deacon leads the Divine Office, Angelus, litany, and novena in the chapel.
Christmas devotions honor the Incarnation and Nativity of the Messiah, born of Mary in Bethlehem.
On the Baptism of the Lord, our pastor baptizes infants with chrism.
Lenten devotions call clergy and laity to repentance, contrition, humility, and penance.
A priest hears sacramental confession, grants absolution, and assigns acts of penance.
The Way of the Cross recalls the Crucifixion and entombment; a Palm Sunday entry and religious procession open Holy Week, and the Last Supper recalls the institution of the Eucharist.
Easter devotions proclaim the Resurrection, Ascension of Christ, and Pentecost, when the Paraclete descended.
Through RCIA, adults receive baptism, chrismation, and Holy Communion.
Our diocesan bishop confers confirmation at the cathedral; an auxiliary bishop ordains a transitional deacon through Holy Orders.
Healing sacraments continue year-round.
Our chaplain brings last anointing to the hospital chapel, and reconciliation restores communion.
Matrimony unites each spouse in Christian marriage.
A funeral ends with burial, interment, or cremation in a consecrated cemetery.

This bulletin cites Scripture, the Decalogue, the Beatitudes, and Catholic social teaching on faith, hope, chastity, prudence, justice, and forgiveness, so that patience, meekness, and compassion guide every family.
We pray the Holy Rosary, Hail Mary, Memorare, and Glory Be during Eucharistic adoration of the Blessed Sacrament, honoring the Trinity.
Every volunteer, donor, benefactor, trustee, secretary, and treasurer helps.
A religious sister, prior, and nun from a nearby monastery, abbey, convent, and friary join our youth minister, church rector, and lay minister at the basilica and shrine.
Our seminary, college, and parish church welcome each immigrant and refugee from Italy, Ireland, Mexico, and Poland.
We remain in communion with the Pope, the Holy See, our archbishop, and the universal church.

THE LITURGICAL YEAR AT SAINT JOSEPH PARISH
Our parish community keeps the liturgical year through liturgy, devotion, worship, adoration, and charity, guided by church law and papal law. Pastor, parish vicar, deacon, catechist, sponsor, and laity share each Mass and rite.

Advent devotions begin the year. Each catechist prepares every child, parent, and student for baptism, confirmation, and Eucharist, while our permanent deacon leads the Divine Office, Angelus, litany, and novena in the chapel.

Christmas devotions honor the Incarnation and Nativity of the Messiah, born of Mary in Bethlehem. On the Baptism of the Lord, our pastor baptizes infants with chrism.

Lenten devotions call clergy and laity to repentance, contrition, humility, and penance. A priest hears sacramental confession, grants absolution, and assigns acts of penance. The Way of the Cross recalls the Crucifixion and entombment; a Palm Sunday entry and religious procession open Holy Week, and the Last Supper recalls the institution of the Eucharist.

Easter devotions proclaim the Resurrection, Ascension of Christ, and Pentecost, when the Paraclete descended. Through RCIA, adults receive baptism, chrismation, and Holy Communion. Our diocesan bishop confers confirmation at the cathedral; an auxiliary bishop ordains a transitional deacon through Holy Orders.

Healing sacraments continue year-round. Our chaplain brings last anointing to the hospital chapel, and reconciliation restores communion. Matrimony unites each spouse in Christian marriage. A funeral ends with burial, interment, or cremation in a consecrated cemetery.

This bulletin cites Scripture, the Decalogue, the Beatitudes, and Catholic social teaching on faith, hope, chastity, prudence, justice, and forgiveness, so that patience, meekness, and compassion guide every family. We pray the Holy Rosary, Hail Mary, Memorare, and Glory Be during Eucharistic adoration of the Blessed Sacrament, honoring the Trinity.

Every volunteer, donor, benefactor, trustee, secretary, and treasurer helps. A religious sister, prior, and nun from a nearby monastery, abbey, convent, and friary join our youth minister, church rector, and lay minister at the basilica and shrine. Our seminary, college, and parish church welcome each immigrant and refugee from Italy, Ireland, Mexico, and Poland. We remain in communion with the Pope, the Holy See, our archbishop, and the universal church.
